headline: Run large language models at home, BitTorrent-style
summary: This new approach allows users to host and share LLMs on their personal devices, leveraging a decentralized network for distribution and access.
details: A novel approach is emerging that allows users to host and run large language models (LLMs) directly on their home computers. This method leverages a peer-to-peer network, similar to how BitTorrent distributes files, to make powerful AI accessible without relying on centralized cloud providers.

This decentralized model aims to democratize access to advanced AI capabilities, enabling individuals and smaller organizations to experiment with and deploy LLMs more freely. It could significantly reduce computational costs and data privacy concerns associated with commercial AI services.

By distributing the computational load and model data across a network of user devices, the system enhances resilience and scalability. Participants contribute their local resources, collectively forming a robust infrastructure for LLM operations.

This paradigm shift could foster innovation in AI development, allowing for more diverse and experimental applications. It also presents a potential pathway for open-source LLMs to gain wider adoption and community-driven improvement.

headline_marked: [[Lego’s Donkey Kong arcade machine lets Mario jump endless barrels]] — Miyamoto is reportedly happy
headline: Lego’s Donkey Kong arcade machine lets Mario jump endless barrels — Miyamoto is reportedly happy
summary: The $200 set, designed by Carl Merriam, features a fully functional game with a joystick and jump button, releasing August 1st.
details: Lego has unveiled a new $200 Donkey Kong arcade machine set, designed by Carl Merriam, known for other nostalgic Lego sets. The set reportedly has the approval of Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto himself, and is set to release on August 1st.
While not a digital replica, the set features a basic, fully functional game. It includes a working joystick for Mario (Jumpman) to move left and right, and a button for him to leap over obstacles.

Players can release an endless series of barrels by pulling a lever. These are the original barrels from Lego's 1989 pirate sets, and designer Carl Merriam spent significant time ensuring they roll slowly without getting stuck.

Nintendo specifically requested that poison barrels be heavier, so Lego added Minifigure heads inside them. The barrel mechanism is a pump system, holding 20 barrels in total, allowing up to 6 to roll down simultaneously.

The barrels roll from top to bottom into a hopper, which feeds them back into the pump, creating an infinite loop. The biggest design challenge was achieving the slow, consistent barrel roll, solved by combining various Lego elements.
The joystick moves Jumpman via a long lever and "dingler" mechanism, while the jump button uses a piano-key-like see-saw lever to lift Jumpman. Gravity returns him to the bottom after a jump.

Lego's new $200 Donkey Kong arcade machine is a fully functional game, complete with a joystick and endless barrels.

Players can release an endless series of barrels by pulling a lever. These are the original barrels from Lego's 1989 pirate sets, and designer Carl Merriam spent significant time ensuring they roll slowly without getting stuck.

Nintendo specifically requested that poison barrels be heavier, so Lego added Minifigure heads inside them. The barrel mechanism is a pump system, holding 20 barrels in total, allowing up to 6 to roll down simultaneously.

The barrels roll from top to bottom into a hopper, which feeds them back into the pump, creating an infinite loop. The biggest design challenge was achieving the slow, consistent barrel roll, solved by combining various Lego elements.

The joystick moves Jumpman via a long lever and "dingler" mechanism, while the jump button uses a piano-key-like see-saw lever to lift Jumpman. Gravity returns him to the bottom after a jump.
